subject: Renewal runbook: staggered top-up, co-term optionality & rollback window
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@tidalai.com>, procurement@tidalai.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal runbook: staggered top-up, co-term optionality & rollback window

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion I put together a short runbook for the renewal/expansion path we talked about. Attaching the proposal PDF for reference (Tidal_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf). High level: 

- Staged top-up: add 30% additional committed units in month 1, 40% in month 2, 30% in month 3. This smooths billing and avoids a large one-time invoice.
- Rollback window: a 14-day rollback following month 3 where you can reduce the committed level by up to 15% and receive a partial credit for unused reserved units.
- True-up waterfall: usage above committed during the three-month period will be billed at standard overage rates; any sustained over-usage triggers an automatic rebaseline conversation (no surprise invoices).
- Co-term option: you can elect to co-term to Jan 31, 2027 at a blended rate (we show a pro-rata path in the attached).

Questions for you (so we can finalize legal/procurement):
1) Is procurement expecting a single PO for the whole staged amount or month-by-month POs?
2) Do you need invoice timing aligned with calendar month or with PO date?
3) Will Tidal want the co-term locked now, or do you prefer to convert after the three-month pilot if usage normalizes?

If useful I can also provide an invoice schedule mock and a short one-pager for your finance team. Next steps from our side: prepare the SOW amendment for legal to redline (I'll attach a draft) and generate the DocuSign envelope once PO timing is confirmed.

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Tidal_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@tidalai.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal runbook: staggered top-up, co-term optionality & rollback window

Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifying items from procurement and finance: 

- Rollback mechanics: when you say "partial credit" can you quantify (is it credit back to next invoice, or a refund)? Any minimum notice to invoke rollback?
- If we choose month-by-month POs, will the discount tier stay the same as the staged total? We want to avoid losing the uplift discount if we buy incrementally.
- Co-term: leaning toward locking co-term now if the blended rate is a demonstrable saving — can you share the blended math and what happens to unused credits at co-term?

Procurement prefers an attached SOW they can redline and a sample invoice schedule. Can you confirm timeline — we target sign-off before EOD Friday (internal ask but may be tight).

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Platform Ops
Tidal AI
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@tidalai.com>, procurement@tidalai.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal runbook: staggered top-up, co-term optionality & rollback window

Elena — thanks, good questions. Short answers below and I attached the SOW amendment draft for legal (SOW_amendment_draft.docx). I'll also drop the invoice mock into the DocuSign once we confirm PO cadence.

- Rollback credit: If rollback is invoked within the 14-day window we issue a credit applied to your next invoice. Example: if you committed to +300k tokens across the staged months and rollback reduces committed to +255k (15% reduction), we'll credit 45k worth of reserved-unit cost at the blended committed rate back to the next invoice. We typically don't do cash refunds for credits under $5k unless agreed in writing.
- Notice: 5 business days' written notice is required to invoke the rollback during the 14-day window — that gives us time to adjust capacity reservations and billing.
- Discount preservation for month-by-month POs: we can offer a commitment-preservation clause in the SOW — if you follow the staged top-up map within the three-month window, discounting remains at the staged-tier level even if procurement issues separate POs. We'll document the exact PO numbers to match.
- Co-term unused credits: if you opt to co-term at Jan 31, 2027 and there are unused reserved-unit credits, those credits can be carried forward through the co-term date but are forfeited after the co-term unless you renew again. We'll show the exact treatment in the amendment.

Action items: 
- Naomi: can you prepare the invoice mock (month-by-month vs single PO) and the DocuSign envelope?
- Marissa: can you confirm any finance approval limits we should flag if the blended discount goes beyond 15%?

Elena — if you confirm PO cadence (single vs month-by-month) by EOD Thursday we should be able to get the envelope ready for signature before Friday close.

Best,
Ben

Attachments: SOW_amendment_draft.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal runbook: staggered top-up, co-term optionality & rollback window

Internal note — looping in approval guardrails before we present. 

- Discount cap: finance has a standard approval threshold of 15% for mid-contract upsells without VP approval. Anything above 15% needs revenue ops + VP sign-off. We can offer up to 15% in the envelope today.
- Rollback window: two weeks (14 days) is fine; recommend we keep the 5-business-day notice ask so operations can adjust.
- PO timing: prioritize a single PO if procurement can do it — reduces administrative overhead. If they must do monthly POs, ensure we attach the commitment-preservation clause and list PO numbers in SOW.

Ben — offer the 14-day rollback and set the discount in DocuSign to 15% max. If Tidal requests more, escalate to me and I will route to ops. Naomi, please draft the invoice mock and prepare the DocuSign envelope with the two options (single PO / monthly PO) and include the blended-rate table.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
